terms.gloss: on the way, on one’s way
terms.register: vōx sermōnis cotīdiānī: Plaut., Ter.; Cic. in epistulīs
evidence: Ter. Eun. 4.2.1: dum rūs eō, coepī egomet mēcum inter viās (Lewis & Short s.v. inter)
Cic. Att. 4.3.5: sī sē inter viam obtulerit (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Literally “among the roads”: Latin puts the traveller between the roads.

terms.latin: iter habēre (+ accusative of the place, or ad)
terms.gloss: be on one’s way to, be heading for
evidence: Caes. BC 3.106.1: Caesar conjectāns eum Aegyptum iter habēre (Lewis & Short s.v. conjectō)
terms.comment: Caesar has the bare accusative of a country, Aegyptum; ad goes with a town or person.

sources: Lewis & Short: inter
Lewis & Short: iter
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
